title.narrative: Assam State Public Finance Institutional Reforms (ASPIRe) Project

description.narrative: 13. The Project Development Objective (PDO) is: 'to contribute to improvement in predictability and transparency in budget execution and efficiency in tax administration in Assam.'The key beneficiaries of the project will include: the Finance Department, Office of Commissioner of Taxes, Department of Excise and Department of Information Technology; procuring agencies in select line departments and government officials. All line departments, directorates and field level units will benefit from having information of budge execution rates and status of payment of bills. The project will also benefit the citizens of Assam through efficient processes and better service delivery provided by public institutions (such as electronic payments and collections for services, better public procurement and enhanced tax payer services) and enhanced transparency.

condition.narrative: Finance Agreement :DLIs Verification and Withdrawals | Description :For withdrawals for eligible expenditures under Component 2.2of the Project, the Borrower, through Assam, shall: (i) carry out a verification process to certify fulfillment of DLI Targetsguided by a DLI Verification Protocol agreed with the Bank; (ii) furnish to the Bank the corresponding verification reports in formand substance acceptable to the Bank, in order to submit evidence satisfactory to the Bank of the achievement of the DLIs; and(iii) furnish to the Bank the applicable interim unaudited financial reports documenting the incurrence of eligible expenditures. |Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Project Management Unit | Description :Assam shall maintain the Assam Society for Comprehensive FinancialManagement System (AS-CFMS) as the Project Management Unit (PMU) for the Project with functions and responsibilities acceptable tothe Bank, and: (i) ensure that the AS-CFMS is led by a State project director from the Indian Administrative Services (IAS) andassisted by an additional project director from the IAS/Assam Civil Services and adequate professional and administrative staff;and (ii) ensure that, for each component/sub-component of the Project, a coordinator from other implementing departments of Assamis designated to coordinate with the PMU on the implementation of activities, monitoring, and reporting. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Retroactive Financing | Description :No withdrawal shall be made for payments made prior to the date of signingof the Loan Agreement, except that the Borrower may withdraw for payments made before such date but on or after August 1, 2016 upto: (i) an amount not to exceed US$ 1,000,000 for eligible expenditures under Components 1, 2.1 and 3 of the Project; and (ii) anamount not to exceed US$ 3,000,000 for eligible expenditures under Component 2.2 of the Project. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Reversal of DLIs | Description :In the event a reversal of a DLI Target, which has already been verified and forwhich the corresponding disbursements have been made by the Bank, has occurred in a manner that would, in the opinion of the Bank,adversely affect the achievement of the objectives of the Project, the Borrower shall refund the disbursements already made by theBank for such DLI Target. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement: Other Undertaking: Ensure inter alia that the Project's activities involving collection, storage, usage, and/orprocessing of personal data are carried out with due regard to the Borrower's existing legal framework and appropriateinternationaldata protection and privacy standards and practices. Frequency: CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement: Safeguards: ensure that the obligation to comply with the EMP is incorporated in the contracts between theProject Implementing Entity and the relevant contractors and any entity supervising the Project's civil works and undertake toprepare and disclose the EMP and any related safeguard document prior to the commencement of civil works. Frequency: CONTINUOUS

title.narrative: Reduction in cost of collection of tax revenue in Excise Department
Reduction in share of discretionary expenditure reported in the last quarter of the financial year
Enhanced services provided by Excise Department using e-Governance

baseline.value: All procedures and processes are manual in the Excise Department; Excise revenue INR 807 crore in 2015-2016

target.value: Enhanced services provided by the Excise Department and 80% increase in excise revenue over baseline

actual.value: The new E-Gov solution rolled out and linked to GoA's Ease of Doing Business Portal. Track and Trace module implemented in the bottling plants in the state. Excise revenue has increased 300 percent from the baseline of FY2016 to FY2024.

title.narrative: Increased percentage of e-collection and e-payments using common e-collection and payment systems

baseline.value: E-collection for Excise NIL;for the CoT 35% by volume for VAT and nil for other taxes; andfragmented systems and low base of e-payments

target.value: At least 90% of excise and 80% of non-GST tax (administered by the COT) collected electronically and at least 80% of payments made electronically by the treasuries and e-collection portal scaled up to cover additional services

actual.value: (i) Over 90 percent payments by the treasuries are digital using RBI's e-kuber platform; and (ii) over 95 percent of excise revenue and Non GST tax collection is being collected electronically using e-Gras; which has also been extended to 684 non tax revenue collections

title.narrative: Enhanced services provided by office of the Commissioner of Taxes (CoT) using e-Governance

baseline.value: Fragmented and outdatedIT applications; e-return filing at 15% for VAT; e-returns do not have in-built electronic scrutiny feature;No e-governance solutions for non GST State taxes

target.value: Enhanced taxpayer services provided by CoT for returns, obligations, and communication

actual.value: a new integrated IT application for all non-GST tax revenues administered by CoT has been rolled out and tax payer services e-enabled reducing interface.

title.narrative: Enhanced capacity in Cash and Debt Management

baseline.value: Fragmented institutions fordebt management;absence of active cashand debt management andcash-flow forecasting

target.value: Cash and Debt Management Unit established;Annual borrowing informed by cash-flow forecasts; Enhanced disclosures on public debt Public debt data digitized

actual.value: Public Debt statistics and performance has been reported in the statement under Assamâ€™s FRBM Act by the Finance Department. Complete Public Debt data has been recorded in the Debt Management Module of Fin Assam portal.

baseline.value: GO issued for mandatory e-Procurement for procurement above INR 20 lacs; e-Procurement tender value in 2015Ã¢Â€Â€2016 - INR 5,700 crores.

target.value: Increased coverage of value of e-procurement (250% increase over baseline); enhanced disclosure and transparency in procurement.

actual.value: e-procurement in FY 2023-24 was 9726 tenders with a value of Rs 37,012 crores which is a 600 percent increase over the baseline value. (ii) SPPP is operational

title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity in office of the Commissioner of Taxes (CoT)

baseline.value: Inadequate audit systems that is, lack of system based audit selection and limited tax analyticalcapacity

target.value: Capacity of core tax administration functions strengthened

actual.value: The CTD has established an Economic Intelligence Unit (EIU) and enhanced its data analytics capability using data analytics software and forensic tools. Based on preliminary data analytics, CTD has realized over INR 240 crores in GST revenue in FY 2023-24. Model Audit Manual as prepared by GST Council adopted by Govt. of Assam

title.narrative: Enhanced public disclosure of budget information and Citizen's Engagement

target.value: Enhanced budget disclosure to citizens, including compliance with the disclosure requirements of the Assamâ€™s FRBM Act

actual.value: Disclosures made by Finance Department further complying with the requirements of the Assamâ€™s FRBM Act by disclosing the impact of supplementary demand for grants on fiscal indicators.

title.narrative: Strengthened public procurement framework and capacity building of officials (of which 5% are female)

baseline.value: Outdated procurement rules; no SBDs; and no system for public procurement training

target.value: Procurement framework strengthened by approval of procurement rules and notification SBDs; and capacity of selected officials enhanced (1000 officials trained in public procurement)

actual.value: (i) Procurement rules and seven SBD's have been notified by the GoA; (ii) Cumulatively 1613 officials have been trained in procurement of which 306 (19 percent) are female. (iiI) The MOOC for procurement has been launched and 1555 officials have registered for the same

title.narrative: Enhanced controls in budget execution and reporting

baseline.value: Processes for budget distribution, budget control, and bill submission by the DDOs are manual; No decision support for Finance Department and delays in submission of monthly accounts for compilation.

target.value: Controls over Budget distribution and execution and accounting / reporting strengthened through a functional and integrated FMIS and decision support system for the FD operationalized

actual.value: (i) Core FMIS modules relating to budget preparation and distribution, payroll, bill submission and expenditure processing and reporting have been fully rolled out and legacy systems retired as of March 31, 2024. Integrations completed with four key external systems. (ii) The timely submission of monthly accounts to the AG achieved by all the accounts rendering units, as of March 31, 2024.

title.narrative: Training of GoA officials in PFM (of which 10% are female)

target.value: Enhanced PFM capacity of the GoA's finance officials in selected areas of PFM (500 officials trained)

actual.value: Cumulatively 904 officials have been trained of which 135 (15 percent) are female.

title.narrative: Public access to key budget execution reports (Yes/No)
Digitization and improving efficiency in payment processes for selected State DBT schemes through establishment of a Centralized IT Platform

baseline.value: Fragmented scheme- based MIS systems and largely manual processes

target.value: Centralized IT platform for State DBT schemes operational with selected schemes on-boarded and using key functionalities

actual.value: The DIDS system is operational and three schemes on-boarded and monthly payments aggregating to US$ 25 million to 2.4 million beneficiaries being made through DIDS.
